title: Whole Turkey (frozen)

drivers.name: Price Increase (6.1%)
drivers.evidence: Same price level in Easter week 2026 (x1.35), but that week had holiday. Recent weeks at same price average 4.5 (18% below baseline); noise-adjusted past promotion lifts are x1.0.

adjustment.analysis: Baseline median is 5.5. Price increased 6.1% to $29.20 (vs. $27.53), a level previously seen during Easter week 2026 (2026-03-30), which sold at x1.35 vs baseline. That week had a holiday, so not fully comparable. No promotion history shows lift above x1.35, and noise-adjusted estimates are x1.0. Recent weeks at $29.20 (2026-03-30 to 2026-04-13) show median 4.5, 18% below baseline—consistent with price sensitivity. No event, promotion, or post-promo effect this week. Classical model suggests no lift, and evidence supports downward pressure. Adjust down to reflect price impact, but shrink toward 1.0 due to limited data. No upside spread needed.

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 5.5 | 5%-95%: 0.0 - 17.3 | 10%-90%: 0.3 - 12.3

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-100% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
